The anti-graft agency claimed that the Lagos State University Teaching Hospital (LASUTH), Ikeja, disowned the report after it contacted the hospital to verify its authenticity.
The EFCC Counsel, Ekene Iheanacho (SAN) made the allegation before Justice Mojisola Dada also alleged that the hospital confirmed in a letter dated July 22 that the medical report, purportedly issued to Ufoma on June 2, 2026, did not come from the institution.

Immanuel faces a two-count charge of obtaining by false pretence and forgery over an alleged $1.5 million investment fraud involving Adebisi Adebutu of R28 Holdings Ltd.
At the resumed hearing of the matter on Monday, Iheanacho told the judge that the prosecution had filed a further counter-affidavit on November 11, attaching the hospital’s response to inform the court of the development.
He added that the defence had been served with the filing that same day.
The prosecutor claimed, “We have written a letter to the management of Lagos State University Teaching Hospital (LASUTH) to confirm the authenticity or otherwise of the medical report attached to the defendant’s bail application.
“We got a response from the hospital stating that the said medical report dated June 2, 2026, is a forged document. It is not authentic,” the lawyer told the court.
The disclosure came as the case was listed for continuation of trial and a hearing on a fresh bail application filed by Immanuel and his company, Intermediate Investment Holdings Ltd.
However, the correctional centre did not produce the defendant in court.
The defence counsel, Wilson Okereke said he needed to confirm the status of the bail application, noting that the lead counsel handling the matter had filed a notice of withdrawal.
Okereke also told the court that new counsel had filed a notice seeking to withdraw the former lead counsel’s application concerning the bail proceedings.
The EFCC had accused the defendant and his company of allegedly obtained the money from Adebutu between April 2022 and October 2023, claiming it would be invested in a proposed petroleum development project.
The commission alleged that the complainant was induced to release the funds by promises of reimbursement, payment of development capital fees and an allocation of shares in Intermediate Investment Holdings Ltd.
The EFCC further accused Immanuel of forging a document titled “Term Sheet”, purportedly executed by Sherrif Oluwo and Olaniran Osotuyi, to facilitate the alleged transaction.
The prosecution said the alleged offences contravene Sections 1(1)(a) and 1(3) of the Advance Fee Fraud and Other Fraud Related Offences Act, 2006, and Section 363 of the Criminal Law of Lagos State, 2015.
Justice Dada adjourned the case until November 18 for continuation of the trial.
